notes: Fix: the motor leads are 'lead' ports and the controller's motor terminals were 'lug' ports, which is not a compatible pair. The motor terminal ports (Motor A and Motor B) are now kind header-socket, which accepts a lead. The connections are unchanged.
Parts are the same as in step 1. No parts were added or dropped.
The battery pack's red lead goes to VIN and its black lead to GND, as the manual requires. The pack must be switched off while this is wired.
The motors can go either way round. Motor 1 is on the Motor B block and motor 2 on the Motor A block. Which motor goes on which block is not specified.

The board plugs straight onto the Pi's GPIO header. The catalogue's rpi-3b card only has a GPIO_HEADER port, so the join is made between the two GPIO_HEADER ports. GPIO 7, 8, 9 and 10 are the pins the board uses.
The motor and battery leads are attached to the motors and the battery pack, so no separate jumper wires are used. They are clamped in the terminal blocks with screws.
The Pi is powered separately (its own USB supply), not from the battery pack.
